name: Cell Density Calculator
seoDesc: Cell density is cells per millilitre of culture, and it decides when to split, how to seed and whether a culture is in log phase. Free cell density calculator
summary:
Cell density is cells per millilitre of culture, and it decides when to split, how to seed and whether a culture is in log phase. It returns cell density, density per area and cells/mL from OD600, and the panel shows all of them at once.

This calculator converts counts, haemocytometer readings and OD600 values into cells/mL and cells/cm². Every result is derived from the boxes you fill in, so changing one input updates the whole panel at once. Units are stated on every box and in every result, so a figure copied out of a protocol, a datasheet or a chart can be entered without converting it first.

sections.title: The formula behind the Cell Density
sections.html:
Cells/mL = (count ÷ squares) × dilution × 10⁴; for E. coli, 1 OD600 ≈ 8 × 10⁸ cells/mL

The symbols in the formula
SymbolWhat it stands forUnit
cells_countedcells countedcells
dilutiondilution before counting×
OD600optical density at 600 nmAU

sections.title: How do I use the Cell Density?
sections.html:
The form asks only for what the formula needs — nothing is optional decoration.

  1. Enter the values you already have. Every box accepts a decimal point and a minus sign; thousands separators are ignored.
  2. The grey boxes are results: they are worked out from your inputs and cannot be typed into.
  3. Press Calculate. The results fill in together, and from then on they follow every edit you make — there is no page to reload and nothing to submit.

sections.title: A worked example
sections.html:
Take the default values the page opens with: cells counted of 300 cells, squares counted of 4, dilution factor of 1 ×, growth area of 25 cm², od600 of 0.6.

Substituting them into the formula gives cell density of 750,000 cells/mL, density per area of 30,000 cells/cm², cells/ml from od600 of 480,000,000 cells/mL.

The arithmetic is the page's own: change one box and the result moves by the amount the formula implies, which is the quickest way to convince yourself the tool is honest.

sections.title: What does the result mean?
sections.html:
A raw figure only means something next to the bands it is normally judged against. Here is the scale that goes with this one:

How to read the result
ResultBandWhat it means
0.6 – 1.0 ×10⁶/mLLowsparse; split less or seed more
1 – 5 ×10⁶/mLLog phasehealthy adherent culture ready to passage
above 10⁷/mLConfluent / stationarysplit now

  • The OD600 conversion is species-specific: 8 × 10⁸ cells/mL per OD unit is a working figure for E. coli, and yeast is roughly 3 × 10⁷.

  • Adherent cultures are usually quoted per cm², suspension cultures per mL; the growth area box converts between them.

  • Confluence is a visual estimate; density is the measurement. They disagree most in heterogeneous cultures.

sections.title: What are the common mistakes?
sections.html:
The arithmetic is simple; the inputs are where things go wrong. The usual culprits:

  • Using OD600 for eukaryotic cells, where it means almost nothing.
  • Reading OD600 above 1.0 without diluting, where the relationship stops being linear.
  • Quoting cells/mL for an adherent culture without the area.

faq.q: What is a normal cell density for a T75 flask?
faq.a: About 1–2 × 10⁶ cells/mL at 80% confluence, or roughly 8 × 10⁴ cells/cm².

faq.q: Why is my OD600 reading not linear?
faq.a: Above about 1.0 the detector saturates; dilute tenfold and multiply.

faq.q: What does the Cell Density actually calculate?
faq.a: It returns cell density, density per area and cells/mL from OD600. Each one is derived by the formula on this page, so you can check any figure by hand.

faq.q: Do I have to fill in every box?
faq.a: Fill in the ones you know. The result boxes are computed from them, so you never enter a value the formula can derive — and if you change an input, every result updates with it.

faq.q: Why is the answer different from the one in my protocol?
faq.a: Nearly always a unit or a rounding difference. This calculator works in the units printed next to each box, keeps full precision internally and only rounds for display, so recomputing from the rounded numbers on screen can differ in the last digit.

faq.q: Can I use it with the numbers straight from a datasheet?
faq.a: Yes. Every box states its unit, and nothing is converted behind your back, so a figure copied from a datasheet, a kit insert or a protocol goes in as printed.
